ai.description: The Indian softshell turtle reaches a carapace length of 94 cm. Its olive-green shell is oval and leathery, featuring a distinct, elongated snout and dark, eye-like ocelli on the dorsal surface.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Nilssonia gangetica* is best distinguished by the presence of four to eight distinct, dark-edged ocelli (eyespots) on its olive-green carapace, unlike other softshells.
ai.habitat: The Indian Softshell Turtle inhabits deep, slow-moving rivers, streams, and lakes with sandy or muddy bottoms, typically found at low-to-moderate altitudes below 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Softshell Turtle is primarily nocturnal, emerging from riverbeds at night to forage for fish, crustaceans, and mollusks in murky waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Indian Softshell Turtle is oviparous, breeding from December to June. Females lay clutches of 8–35 spherical, hard-shelled eggs in nests along riverbanks.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Softshell Turtle inhabits major river systems across northern, central, and peninsular India, ranging from low-lying plains up to 600 meters in elevation.
